case: I'm broke till Friday, no peanuts, tired of rice, want something warm

lines.name: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies

no_label: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
plan.note: Warm, filling, rice-free and peanut-free: Dal (two batches, 8 bowls) plus a pot of homemade baked beans. Dal reheats well, so cook it in big batches. Not priced or not found: salt, pepper, cumin and mustard seeds, ginger, chipotle/chili sauce; Rotel stands in for the green chili and brown sugar for molasses.

case: vegetarian, $20 for the week, I like spicy food

lines.name: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
Kroger® Enriched Long Grain White Rice

no_label: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
plan.note: Dal is cheap, filling and high in protein, and the Rotel (tomatoes with green chilies) gives it a spicy kick. Serve it over plain rice. Cumin seeds, mustard seeds and ginger weren't affordable or available, so they're left out. Salt, pepper and any extra chili flakes aren't priced. You can stir the leftover Rotel into the rice for red rice.

lines.name: Simple Truth Organic® 100% Whole Grain Rolled 1 Minute Oats

plan.note: Both recipes are dairy-free and cheap: a big bag of dried pinto beans makes several protein- and fiber-rich dinners, and apple cinnamon oatmeal covers breakfasts. Cook the beans in bulk and reheat them through the week. Cinnamon isn't priced (use what you have or buy a small jar), and the oats are meant to be cooked in the cider.

Kroger® White Corn Restaurant Style Tortilla Chips
ReaLime 100% Lime Juice, 15 fl oz bottle

no_label: Cal Fresco BBQ Green Onions Bag
ReaLime 100% Lime Juice, 15 fl oz bottle
plan.note: Taco Salad is nut-free, cheap, and travels well, with 3 batches making 6 lunches. I used only this one recipe because the other options need many pricey ingredients or have no ingredient list. Tip: pack the chips and dressing separately so the salad stays crisp until lunch. Salt and pepper aren't priced. The bean option is black beans, and the extra salad toppings are skipped.

lines.name: Kroger® Gluten Free Whole Chipotle Peppers in Adobo Sauce
Kroger® Grade A Large White Eggs
Sargento Off the Block Fine Cut Sharp Cheddar Natural Cheese Shreds

no_label: Kroger® Gluten Free Whole Chipotle Peppers in Adobo Sauce
plan.note: Both recipes are naturally gluten free and filling: bean-based baked beans plus a crustless egg quiche. Cook a big pot of beans once and reheat it through the week. Salt and pepper aren't priced, and you'll have beans, sugar and mustard left over. Check labels on the mustard and cheese for gluten.

case: cheapest possible week of dinners, I eat anything

plan.note: Baked beans from scratch is the cheapest dinner on the list. One 4 lb bag of dried pinto beans covers four batches, which is 8 servings for the week. Cook the beans in a big pot and freeze portions. Mustard, brown sugar and chipotle are bought in small amounts and will last past this week. I left out the other recipes because they would put you over $15. Water isn't priced.

case: I can't eat shellfish or eggs, want some comfort food

lines.name: Jimmy Dean® NEW Premium Turkey Sausage Roll Fresh Regular Ready to Cook
Kroger® Enriched Long Grain White Rice

plan.note: Two cozy, egg- and shellfish-free comfort dishes: a big pot of cabbage rolls (six servings, freezes well) plus smoky baked beans. Cook the dry lentils and rice ahead, and use the leftover tomatoes from the can for the beans. Salt, pepper and water aren't priced; you'll have lots of leftover butter, sugar and garlic.

case: I want to meal prep on Sunday for the whole week

lines.name: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
Kroger® Enriched Long Grain White Rice

no_label: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
plan.note: Dal (2 batches, 8 servings) is cheap, high in protein and fiber, and reheats well; Rainbow Rice (3 batches) is a cheap base, made as red rice twice and green rice once for variety. Eat dal over the rice, and freeze half the portions so they stay fresh. Salt, pepper and cumin seeds aren't priced (the store search only found hair/skin products for cumin), so use ground cumin from home or skip it. Dal contains milk (butter).

case: vegetarian, no soy, I need protein

lines.name: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
Kroger® Grade A Large White Eggs

no_label: ROTEL Original Diced Tomatoes and Green Chilies
plan.note: Dal gives the most protein per dollar (lentils), and eggs add more. Rainbow Rice (red version, using canned tomatoes) is a cheap side for the dal. Not priced: salt, pepper, cumin and mustard seeds (Kroger only showed hair and skin products for these), and fresh ginger, which I left out to stay in budget. Rotel supplies the green chili.

case: sweet breakfast ideas, I hate oatmeal

lines.name: Kroger® Grade A Large White Eggs

plan.note: Banana Pancakes are a sweet, oatmeal-free breakfast, and two batches give about 20 pancakes for the week. I skipped the Chocolate Zucchini Muffins because they contain oats and I couldn't find cocoa powder at Kroger. Leftover pancakes freeze well and reheat in a toaster. Salt isn't priced because it didn't fit the budget; use a pinch from a pantry if you have it. You'll have flour, sugar, butter and milk left over.

case: cheap high protein dinners, I lift weights

lines.name: Kroger® 80/20 Ground Beef Roll 3 LB (Limit 2 at sale price)
Kroger® Grade A Large White Eggs

no_label: Kroger® 80/20 Ground Beef Roll 3 LB (Limit 2 at sale price)
plan.note: Half-Veggie Burgers are the cheapest high-protein dinner in the book, since lentils and ground beef share the load. Cook three batches for 24 burgers. Freeze the extras and reheat them through the week. Salt and pepper aren't priced. Cook the dry lentils first, about 3 cups cooked per batch. I added a carton of eggs for the optional egg. The plan comes close to your protein goal but may fall slightly short on paper at this budget.

case: vegetarian and I want lots of protein

lines.name: Cal Fresco BBQ Green Onions Bag

no_label: Cal Fresco BBQ Green Onions Bag
plan.note: Tofu Hot Pot has the most protein of the recipes (30 g per serving), and cooking it 4 times gives the most protein the budget allows. I skipped mushrooms ($6), garlic, chili paste and sesame oil to stay under budget: add garlic or mushrooms if you have them. Salt, water and other pantry items are unpriced. The plan is still below the 80 g/day goal.
